# ShopHawk Review (2026): Pricing, AI, 3D Inspections & Best Fit

ShopHawk is an all-in-one CRM and shop-management platform built specifically for automotive restyling and protection businesses — including window tint, PPF, ceramic coating, vinyl wrap and detailing.

Its pitch is broader than basic booking software. ShopHawk combines lead management, estimates, work orders, scheduling, invoices, inventory, commissions, 3D vehicle inspections, multi-location reporting and integrations in one system. Its highest plan also adds marketing tools, email and SMS campaigns, review requests and an AI booking assistant.

The positioning is attractive, especially for growing multi-service shops. The important caveat is that ShopHawk is still an early product in the public market, and most of the available evidence comes from ShopHawk's own product pages and vendor-authored comparisons rather than long-term independent testing.

**Research-based · Source check: September 17, 2026**

**Hands-on testing:** Not claimed for this article.

**Affiliate relationship:** DetailerFit did not find a public ShopHawk affiliate or referral program during this source check. Any future commercial relationship will be disclosed and will not change editorial conclusions.

## Quick Verdict

**Our verdict:** Promising specialist CRM with unusually strong scaling tools

**Best for:** Tint, PPF, wrap, ceramic and detailing shops that need stronger lead ownership, operational visibility or multi-location reporting

**Starting price:** $49/month per location

**Most relevant operating plan:** Pro at $149/month per location

**AI plan:** Complete at $199/month per location

**Users:** Unlimited on every published plan

**Core differentiators:** Multi-location dashboards, lead assignment, 3D vehicle inspections, commissions/upsells and broad connected-shop reporting

**Biggest caution:** Limited independent track record and several important capabilities live on higher plans

## Best Fit

ShopHawk is most interesting for an automotive appearance business that has grown beyond simple calendar-and-invoice software.

A solo operator can technically start at $49/month, but the feature set that makes ShopHawk different becomes much more compelling at the $99 Growth and $149 Pro tiers. Shops with several salespeople, installers, bays or locations are the clearest fit because lead assignment, work orders, commissions, inspections and organization-level reporting become more valuable as operational complexity rises.

For a brand-new mobile detailer that mainly needs online booking, basic quotes and invoices, a simpler or cheaper platform may be enough.

## What Is ShopHawk?

ShopHawk is a business-management platform built for automotive restyling and protective-service shops.

The current product targets businesses offering:

- Window tint
- Paint protection film
- Ceramic coating
- Vinyl wrap
- Auto detailing
- Related automotive appearance services

Unlike a generic field-service CRM, ShopHawk is designed around automotive shop workflows. The platform connects leads, customers, proposals, work orders, scheduling, invoices, vehicle inspections, inventory and reporting around the same job record.

That industry-specific focus puts it in the same broad evaluation set as Tint Wiz, Urable, OrbisX, Service VIN, ShopWrk and other automotive appearance platforms rather than only generic products such as Jobber or Housecall Pro.

## ShopHawk Pricing in 2026

ShopHawk currently publishes four plans. Pricing is per location, with unlimited users on every tier.

| Plan | Monthly price | Best description |
|---|---:|---|
| Starter | $49/location | Basic calendar, customers and invoicing |
| Growth | $99/location | CRM, lead pipeline, follow-up and quote tracking |
| Pro | $149/location | Full shop operations, inspections, inventory and reporting |
| Complete | $199/location | Pro plus marketing and AI |

Annual billing currently advertises a 5% discount.

ShopHawk also states there is no setup fee and no long-term contract under the published pricing structure.

### Starter — $49/month per location

Starter includes:

- Calendar
- Clients
- Dashboard
- Invoices
- Unlimited users

This is the entry point, but it does not include the lead pipeline, automated follow-up, work orders, advanced scheduling, inventory or AI features that define the broader ShopHawk platform.

**DetailerFit take:** Starter is inexpensive for a specialist automotive platform, but buyers comparing it with simple mobile-detailing software should focus on what is *not* included as much as the headline price.

### Growth — $99/month per location

Growth adds:

- Leads and CRM pipeline
- Automated follow-ups
- Quote and estimate tracking

This is the first tier that starts to address sales leakage rather than only administration.

**DetailerFit take:** Growth is likely the more meaningful entry point for a shop that wants ShopHawk specifically for lead management.

### Pro — $149/month per location

Pro adds the operational features that make ShopHawk substantially different:

- Work orders
- Scheduling
- Commissions and upsells
- Inventory
- Proposals
- 3D inspections
- Multi-location reporting and KPIs
- Integrations

ShopHawk describes Pro as the full platform except for Marketing and AI.

**DetailerFit take:** For an established tint, PPF, wrap or ceramic shop, Pro is probably the plan to compare most closely with Tint Wiz, Urable and OrbisX.

### Complete — $199/month per location

Complete adds:

- Marketing suite
- AI features
- Email and SMS campaigns
- Review requests
- AI booking assistant

**DetailerFit take:** The value of Complete depends heavily on the production quality of the AI booking workflow and whether the marketing tools replace software the shop already pays for. These features should be tested with real pricing exceptions, scheduling conflicts and edge-case customer questions before becoming the primary front-office workflow.

## Leads, CRM and Automated Follow-Up

ShopHawk's Growth plan introduces a structured lead pipeline, automated follow-up and quote/estimate tracking.

This matters because a common failure point in tint, PPF, ceramic and detailing sales is not creating the quote — it is consistently following up after the quote.

ShopHawk's public product examples show leads moving through a sales funnel and automated messages being used to re-engage prospects.

For shops with several salespeople, ShopHawk also promotes native lead assignment, including round-robin or direct salesperson routing.

**Why it matters:** Lead ownership becomes much more important when inbound volume increases. A shared inbox without ownership can still lose leads if everyone assumes someone else is handling the prospect.

## Work Orders and Scheduling

Pro adds work orders and scheduling.

ShopHawk shows a stage-based work-order board with jobs moving through statuses such as:

- Scheduled
- In Progress
- Awaiting QC
- Ready for Delivery
- Delivered

For a multi-bay tint, wrap, PPF or ceramic operation, that workflow is more useful than a basic appointment calendar because the business needs to know not only *when* the car is arriving, but also where the job sits operationally.

The public product examples also show bay-oriented scheduling and technician assignment.

## 3D Vehicle Inspections

One of ShopHawk's most interesting published features is its 3D vehicle inspection workflow on Pro and Complete.

The system is positioned as a way to document vehicle condition before installation work begins and flag issues against areas of the vehicle.

That could be useful for:

- Existing scratches or chips before PPF
- Paint defects before ceramic coating
- Damage documentation before wrap installation
- Customer sign-off
- Upsell identification
- Reducing disputes over pre-existing damage

### Important distinction

ShopHawk's published 3D inspection tool should not automatically be treated as equivalent to Urable's 3D visualizer.

Urable is strongly associated with vehicle-specific visual selling and coverage visualization. ShopHawk currently emphasizes inspection and condition documentation.

Buyers should test both products directly if 3D workflows are a major purchasing reason.

## Inventory

Inventory is included on Pro and Complete.

This is important because generic CRMs often treat inventory like standard products, while tint, PPF and wrap shops may need more specialized material tracking.

However, ShopHawk's public material does not yet document film-roll workflows with the same level of detail that Tint Wiz publishes for roll weight/length tracking or that some PPF-focused platforms publish for roll and batch control.

**What to ask in a demo:**

- Can partial film rolls be tracked?
- Can material usage be assigned to an individual job?
- Are batch/lot numbers supported?
- Can film cost flow into job profitability?
- Are low-stock alerts supported?
- Can multiple brands and film lines be handled cleanly?

Do not assume a feature labeled “inventory” means the same thing across every automotive platform.

## Commissions and Upsells

ShopHawk includes commissions and upsell tracking on Pro and Complete.

The public interface examples show employee-level upsell performance and service add-ons such as paint correction, ceramic upgrades and tint upgrades.

This is an underrated differentiator for shops with dedicated salespeople or installers who are compensated partly on production or upsells.

A shop should confirm:

- Whether commissions can use different rules by employee
- Whether commissions can be based on gross revenue, profit or service type
- How refunds and discounts affect commissions
- Whether commission reporting integrates with payroll

## Multi-Location Reporting

Multi-location management is one of ShopHawk's clearest positioning points.

The product publishes location-level and organization-level dashboards for revenue, jobs and KPIs.

That makes ShopHawk especially relevant for a business that is moving from one shop to two or more locations and wants management visibility without manually combining spreadsheets.

The value here is less obvious for a one-person mobile detailer, but potentially substantial for a growing restyling group.

## Integrations

ShopHawk currently promotes integrations or connected workflows involving:

- Stripe
- Square
- QuickBooks
- CARFAX
- Meta
- RingCentral
- Twilio
- Yelp
- Dialpad
- Zapier
- Google Ads

The vendor describes payments, accounting, calls, texts, ads and vehicle history writing back into the same shop workflow.

### What to verify before switching

“Integration” can mean anything from a deep two-way sync to a simple connection.

Ask exactly which objects sync and in which direction:

- Customers
- Leads
- Estimates
- Invoices
- Payments
- Vehicle data
- Calls
- Texts
- Ad leads
- Accounting categories
- Inventory

This is especially important for QuickBooks and payments because partial integrations can still leave duplicate-entry work.

## AI Booking Assistant and Marketing Tools

ShopHawk's Complete plan adds its AI and marketing layer.

Published features include:

- AI booking assistant
- Email campaigns
- SMS campaigns
- Review requests
- Broader AI features

This puts ShopHawk into a fast-growing category alongside platforms trying to automate the automotive appearance front office.

The strategic question is no longer simply “Does the CRM have online booking?”

It is increasingly:

**Can the system respond to a lead, understand the vehicle and service request, quote or qualify correctly, find an appropriate slot, collect the next step and hand the job into operations without creating another manual task?**

ShopHawk's Complete plan appears built around that direction.

### What to test before trusting the AI

Use real edge cases:

- Customer gives only a make, not model/year
- Customer asks for a discount
- Customer requests an unsupported film brand
- PPF lead asks for partial coverage
- Customer changes vehicle after receiving a quote
- Appointment requires a two-day bay reservation
- Existing customer asks about a warranty issue
- Customer wants a service combination that conflicts with shop rules

AI booking is only valuable if it knows when *not* to improvise.

## Data Migration and Onboarding

ShopHawk's public FAQ states that new accounts receive a free 15-minute onboarding call.

Its demo page also specifically promotes data-migration planning with the sales team.

However, the public site does not provide enough detail to assume that full historical migration is included in every plan or that every data type from Tint Wiz, Urable, OrbisX or another platform can be imported automatically.

Before cancelling an existing system, ask ShopHawk for a migration test covering:

- Customer records
- Vehicles
- Historical jobs
- Estimates and invoices
- Payments
- Notes
- Photos/files
- Warranties
- Custom fields
- Message history

## ShopHawk vs Tint Wiz

Tint Wiz is still the more established specialist option for tint-heavy businesses, particularly where film inventory and tint-specific proposals are central.

ShopHawk becomes more interesting when the buyer cares about:

- Multi-location dashboards
- Structured lead ownership
- Broader financial/KPI visibility
- Commission tracking
- Lower initial entry pricing

Tint Wiz remains especially compelling for:

- Film-roll inventory
- Tint-first workflows
- Automotive plus flat-glass tint
- Mature project/proposal workflows
- A flat subscription with unlimited users

**Key decision:** Is your business primarily trying to manage film installation more deeply, or manage the whole organization and sales pipeline more deeply?

## ShopHawk vs Urable

Urable is a strong automotive-specific platform with mature vehicle tooling, visual workflows, inspections and broad detailing/restyling operations.

ShopHawk's most obvious strategic advantages are its emphasis on:

- Lead ownership and routing
- Multi-location KPI dashboards
- Sales visibility
- Commissions and upsells
- Lower published entry price

Urable deserves particular attention when detailed vehicle-centric workflow and visual selling are major priorities.

**Key decision:** Do you value vehicle-specific operational depth most, or centralized sales and multi-location management?

## ShopHawk vs OrbisX

OrbisX is one of the more feature-dense platforms in the automotive appearance category and already emphasizes AI-assisted booking, marketing automation, reviews, loyalty and broad operations.

ShopHawk positions itself as a simpler route to:

- Multi-location management
- Organization-level reporting
- Automated lead assignment
- A lower $49 entry point
- A tiered path from CRM to full operations and AI

ShopHawk's own comparison pages favor ShopHawk on those points, but those pages are vendor-authored. Buyers should verify equivalent workflows in live demos of both products.

**Key decision:** Do you want a feature-dense established automation stack, or a newer system built heavily around sales ownership and multi-location management?

## ShopHawk Pros

- Built specifically for automotive restyling and protection shops
- Public pricing is transparent
- Entry price starts at $49/month
- Unlimited users on all published plans
- No published long-term contract
- Lead CRM and automated follow-up from Growth
- Work orders and scheduling on Pro
- 3D vehicle inspections
- Commissions and upsell tracking
- Multi-location reporting
- Broad integration list
- AI booking and marketing available on Complete
- Supports tint, PPF, wrap, ceramic and detailing in one platform

## ShopHawk Cons

- Public independent track record is still limited
- Many of the strongest operational features require Pro at $149/month
- AI and marketing require Complete at $199/month
- Inventory documentation is not yet as detailed publicly as some film-focused competitors
- AI performance needs real-world testing
- Integration depth should be confirmed individually
- Migration scope is not fully documented publicly
- No public affiliate/referral program was found during this review
- Much of the current competitive evidence is vendor-authored

## Who Should Test ShopHawk?

### Put ShopHawk on your demo list if:

- You run tint, PPF, wrap, ceramic and/or detailing
- Your leads are falling through the cracks
- You need clear salesperson ownership
- You have several technicians or bays
- You want work-order stages instead of only appointments
- You need commission or upsell tracking
- You are expanding to multiple locations
- You want stronger business-level reporting
- You want to test an automotive-specific AI booking workflow

### Consider another platform first if:

- You only need basic booking and invoicing
- You are a very small mobile operator with low lead volume
- Film-roll inventory depth is your most important requirement
- You need dedicated PPF/tint pattern cutting
- You prioritize a long independent operating history
- You already have a CRM plus AI receptionist stack that works well

## Final Verdict

### A serious new contender for growing automotive appearance shops

ShopHawk is more interesting than a generic new CRM because the product is clearly designed around the actual economics and workflow of an automotive appearance operation.

The strongest reasons to watch it are not the basic calendar or invoice features. They are the combination of lead ownership, automated follow-up, work orders, commissions, 3D inspections, organization-level reporting and a path into AI-assisted booking.

The pricing is also unusually transparent for a newer industry-specific product.

The main reason for caution is equally clear: ShopHawk's public evidence is still dominated by its own product pages and comparison content. A shop should verify migration, inventory depth, integration behavior and AI edge cases before replacing an established system.

**DetailerFit assessment:** ShopHawk deserves a place on the shortlist for growth-oriented tint, PPF, wrap, ceramic and detailing shops — especially teams that are starting to outgrow a simple booking CRM or need better visibility across salespeople and locations.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much does ShopHawk cost?

ShopHawk currently publishes four monthly plans per location: Starter at $49, Growth at $99, Pro at $149 and Complete at $199. Unlimited users are included on every published tier. Annual billing currently advertises a 5% discount.

### Does ShopHawk have AI?

Yes. ShopHawk's Complete plan currently lists AI features, an AI booking assistant, email and SMS campaigns and review requests.

### Does ShopHawk support PPF and window tint?

Yes. ShopHawk explicitly targets window tint, PPF, ceramic coating, vinyl wrap, detailing and related automotive restyling businesses.

### Does ShopHawk include 3D vehicle inspections?

Yes. 3D inspections are currently listed on the Pro and Complete plans.

### Is ShopHawk good for multi-location shops?

Multi-location reporting and KPIs are one of ShopHawk's main published differentiators and are included on Pro and Complete.

### Does ShopHawk charge per user?

Not under the current published pricing. ShopHawk advertises unlimited users on every plan and charges per location.

### Does ShopHawk have an affiliate program?

DetailerFit did not find a public affiliate or referral program during the September 17, 2026 source check. Direct partnership outreach is currently the most practical route.
